summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, type II diabetes, and a history of recurrent dialysis line infections was admitted after her hemodialysis catheter clotted during a routine session. She reported feeling generally unwell and mildly short of breath but denied fever or other acute symptoms. A temporary femoral line was placed in the emergency department, and alteplase was administered to restore function to the occluded catheter, which was successful. She remained afebrile with negative blood cultures and continued her six-week course of intravenous vancomycin for MRSA vertebral osteomyelitis diagnosed in a prior admission. Chest imaging showed no pulmonary edema or infection. Her dialysis access was restored without surgical intervention, and she completed a dialysis session before discharge. She was transferred to extended care to complete her antibiotic therapy with outpatient follow-up planned.
